newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Airways boss asked to stay on.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Airways boss asked to stay on.

text.p: Cyprus Airways chairman Vassilis Rologis, who resigned last month, will be asked to stay on by the government, Cypriot officials said on Wednesday.

"There are a series of pending issues at the airline and immediate decisions have to be taken by the board of directors in the next months," Cypriot government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides told journalists.
"The President of the Republic plans to ask Mr. Rologis to remain in his seat for the next few months," he said.

Rologis, a non-executive chairman appointed in July 1993, tendered his resignation last month after his election as chairman of the Cyprus Chamber of Commerce and Industry. The government asked that he stay on until a replacement was found.
Rologis is currently travelling abroad and was not available for comment.
One of the toughest issues Cyprus Airways faces is the government's move earlier this year to deregulate flights from Britain and Russia.
This is expected to have a significant impact on the airline's earnings.
The government has an 80 percent stake in Cyprus Airways, with the remaining shares listed on the Cyprus stock exchange.
Nine of the eleven board directors, including the chairman, are appointed by the government.
